Bezier connector between interval edges

Source: R/seq_connector.R
seq_connector.Rd

Draws a cubic Bezier from the left or right edge of one interval to the left or right edge of another, with handles pointing away from each edge. Intervals may sit on the same track or on different tracks. Use it to join consecutive pieces of an assembly, a rearranged chromosome or a read path.

Usage

seq_connector(
  data = NULL,
  mapping = NULL,
  t0 = NULL,
  t1 = NULL,
  aesthetics = aes(),
  styles = NULL,
  height = 0.5,
  handle = 0.04,
  bulge_height = 0.45,
  layer = c("above", "below"),
  legend = NULL,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Optional GRanges or data.frame.

mapping

Optional map().

t0, t1

Track identifiers. Locked to the parent track when added inside a seq_track().

aesthetics

Optional aes(): color, linetype, linewidth for unstyled connectors.

styles

Optional named list of list(col, lty, lwd).

height

Block height as a fraction of the panel inner height (default 0.5).

handle

Handle length as a fraction of the track inner width (default 0.04; same-track handles use 30 percent of it).

bulge_height

Same-track bulge as a fraction of the panel inner height (default 0.45).

layer

"above" (default) or "below" the track elements.

legend

Optional LegendKey, list of keys or seq_legend().

show_legend

Logical. When style is mapped, an automatic legend lists the keys present.

...

Reserved.

Value

A SeqConnectorR6 instance.

Details

Same-track connectors leave from the top (or bottom) edge of blocks of height centred in the panel and bulge up (or down); connectors between tracks leave from the block centres with horizontal handles.

map() fields: x0, x1 (required: the left edges of interval 0 and interval 1, in track coordinates), x0_end, x1_end (right edges; default the left edges), chrom0, chrom1 (window seqnames; required for data.frame data), side0, side1 ("left" or "right"; default "right" and "left"), style (a key into styles) and bulge (same-track only; TRUE or NA up, FALSE down). Numeric edges are used exactly.

Default styles: junction solid blue, inferred red dashed, unused grey. Entries of styles override these by name. A missing or unknown key is drawn with aes(color, linetype, linewidth) (defaults "#3B82D6", 1, 1.3).

Examples

w <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chrA", IRanges::IRanges(0, 100))
df <- data.frame(chrom0 = "chrA", x0 = 10, x0_end = 30,
                 chrom1 = "chrA", x1 = 60, x1_end = 90)
p <- seq_plot() %+%
  seq_track(track_id = "a", windows = w) %+%
  seq_connector(df, map(x0 = x0, x0_end = x0_end, chrom0 = chrom0,
                        x1 = x1, x1_end = x1_end, chrom1 = chrom1),
                t0 = "a", t1 = "a")
